evidence: Applied skill quality-checks.md:14-15 (verify sentence variety, contractions, terse fragments; defect = uniform cadence, marketing gloss, perfectly parallel bullets, voice change between instruction.md and notes). instruction.md reads as a team lead speaking in first person: line 1 'Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day? Two things happen in it.' (question + short fragment-like sentence), 'the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts'; line 3 'tell me why; when it is because a colleague moved that card a moment ago, tell me who. I often move several candidates together'; line 7 'leave my place, my draft and my cursor alone and just tell me there is something new'; line 11 'layout and names are yours. A clear desktop workspace is what matters. We don't need theme switching or a special phone layout.' Contractions present (nobody's, don't, it's, mustn't at lines 1, 11, 13). Sentence length varies from 4-word sentences to long compound ones; no bullets or numbered lists in instruction.md. Grep for gloss terms (seamless|robust|delve|leverage|intuitive|elevate|streamline|empower|ensure|cutting-edge) and em dashes across instruction.md and both notes: zero hits. hireops_rules.md keeps the same 'we/our' owner voice ('our recruiting workspace... what we care about is that the workspace behaves the way this note says' line 3-5; 'Where drafts are kept is yours.' line 175; 'Polling, server-sent events and sockets are all acceptable.' line 123) while using headings/tables appropriate to a rules note, so the voice does not flip between instruction.md and notes. integration.md lines 1-14 are template-controlled boilerplate (byte-identical to the frozen template's integration.md) and are not attributable to the author. Minor observations, not defects: (a) several uncontracted phrasings ('while I am reading', 'it is because', 'A reply I have not sent') give a slightly careful register; (b) instruction.md line 13 is a dense runtime sentence, which the row tolerates because the runtime contract must be stated (row 4); (c) hireops_rules.md section 8 (lines 197-201) is impersonal technical prose ('The runtime may launch Node from a working directory other than the application directory...'), and spelling mixes British 'honour' (instruction.md:13) with American 'honor'/'Honor' (integration.md:7, hireops_rules.md:200) - a small cross-file inconsistency better owned by row 3, not a robotic or LLM voice. Attempted counterexample: a reviewer applying the 'perfectly parallel bullets' defect to hireops_rules.md section 6 'Who takes part' bullets - refuted, because those are a short permission list in a rules note with uneven phrasing ('the others are refused', 'write in none'), not marketing-style parallel copy, and the skill targets the voice of the request, which here is clearly human. No runtime measurement applies to this prose-only row; nothing is missing.
